chain.label: Runway 13 covered with fresh wet snow
chain.trigger: the flight crew saw that the runway was covered with snow, which was inconsistent with their expectations

chain.label: MD-80 susceptibility to rudder blanking at high reverse thrust
chain.trigger: because the engines on MD-80 series airplanes are mounted alongside the tail, high reverse thrust greatly reduces the directional control authority of the rudder

chain.label: Short 7,003-ft runway with Flushing Bay off the departure end and nonstandard safety area
chain.trigger: the presence of Flushing Bay directly off the departure end of the runway

chain.label: LGA runway condition reporting stale; 0903 NOTAM never updated after snow clearing
chain.trigger: the NOTAM that was current at the time of the accident had been issued 2 hours beforehand, and a new NOTAM was not issued after runway snow clearing operations had completed

chain.label: No braking action reports available from dispatch or ATC while en route
chain.trigger: The flight crew also requested braking action reports about 45 and 35 minutes before landing, but none were available at those times

caused_by.evidence: neither had any reports at the time to provide the crew because LGA operations personnel had been conducting snow removal operations on runway 13/31

chain.label: Captain's situational stress about stopping performance
chain.trigger: situational stress resulting from his concerns about stopping performance

caused_by.evidence: The unavailability of braking actions reports and the uncertainty about the runway's condition created some situational stress for the captain
The snowier-than-expected runway...most likely increased the captain's concerns about his ability to stop the airplane within the available runway distance, which exacerbated his situational stress
its relatively short length and the presence of Flushing Bay directly off the departure end of the runway
the ATIS report that was current at the time of the accident (Quebec)...contained outdated and contradictory field condition information about the status of LGA's runways

chain.label: Habitual use of reverse thrust above the 1.3 EPR target despite company training
chain.trigger: despite company training and procedures on EPR targets, more than one-third of the landings captured by the data involved an EPR value of 1.6 or above

chain.label: Captain applied excessive, aggressive reverse thrust (2.07/1.91 EPR vs 1.3 target)
chain.trigger: The maximum EPR values reached during the landing were 2.07 on the left engine and 1.91 on the right engine, which were much higher than the target setting of 1.3 EPR

caused_by.evidence: the circumstances associated with the landing...likely exacerbated the captain's situational stress and prompted him to make an aggressive input on the thrust reversers
a habit of using more than 1.3 EPR might have prevailed when the captain was faced with the demands of the landing on the day of the accident
the captain likely perceived the snowier-than-expected runway as a threat that...could impede his ability to stop the airplane within the available runway length

chain.label: About 9-knot left crosswind component with a slight tailwind
chain.trigger: the controller reported that the wind was from 020º at 10 knots...the crosswind component was about 9 knots

chain.label: Attentional tunneling; captain stopped monitoring the EPR indications
chain.trigger: attentional limitations due to the high workload during the landing, which prevented him from immediately recognizing the use of excessive reverse thrust

caused_by.evidence: the captain was likely experiencing a phenomenon known as 'attentional tunneling,' which refers to the tendency for humans, when highly stressed, to become preoccupied with salient (or threatening) primary cues
multiple distractions during the landing roll: the slide to the left immediately after the application of reverse thrust, concern that the autobrakes were not working

chain.label: Rudder blanked by reverse thrust efflux for about 4.5 seconds
chain.trigger: the rudder was blanked by the thrust reversers, causing the rudder to be ineffective in controlling the airplane's heading

caused_by.evidence: The high EPR values caused rudder blanking...and a subsequent loss of aerodynamic directional control
rudder blanking (which occurs on MD-80 series airplanes when smooth airflow over the rudder is disrupted by high reverse thrust)
All of these factors reduced the captain's monitoring of EPR indications

chain.label: Uncontrollable left yaw to 114º heading during landing roll
chain.trigger: Despite the application of right rudder and right braking, the airplane continued to yaw to the left

caused_by.evidence: the captain was unable to maintain directional control of the airplane due to rudder blanking, which resulted from his application of excessive reverse thrust
a yawing moment resulting from asymmetric reverse thrust (given that the right engine EPR lagged behind the left engine EPR)
a combination of the 9-knot left crosswind component and asymmetric reverse thrust inputs...induced a left yawing moment

chain.label: Airplane departed the left side of runway 13, 3,200 feet from the threshold
chain.trigger: the airplane departed the left side of runway 13 about 1102:30

caused_by.evidence: the airplane's departure from the left side of the runway could not be avoided because directional control was regained too late to be effective

chain.label: Struck retaining wall and perimeter fence; came to rest on embankment, substantial damage
chain.trigger: contacted the airport perimeter fence, and came to rest with the airplane's nose on an embankment next to Flushing Bay

caused_by.evidence: the airplane continued to slide and that the left wing contacted and became caught on a retaining wall for Flushing Bay

chain.label: 29 passengers received minor injuries
chain.trigger: the other 29 passengers received minor injuries

caused_by.evidence: The 2 pilots, 3 flight attendants, and 98 of the 127 passengers were not injured; the other 29 passengers received minor injuries
